executive_assessment.text: Seasonal drought and food-access evidence adds Karo Peli and Dori detail, while the four-province monitoring framework has important station and historical-data gaps.

Four named community anticipatory-action plans add local capacity design. They document intended triggers and support, not delivered aid or measured effects; no climate-terrorism inference is accepted.

geographic_notes.text: FEWS NET assessed Karo Peli at Crisis (IPC Phase 3!) in September 2026, with assistance preventing worse gaps, and projected Phase 3 through January 2027 as poor rainfall, dry spells and low incomes constrain food access.

FEWS NET identifies insecurity and armed-group attacks as the main constraint on household food and income access in the north and east; attacks disrupt market supply and displaced 11,316 people in August 2026.

UNICEF's early-2026 appeal identifies highest nutrition severity in Liptako, Soum, Koulsé, Goulmou, Tapoa, Sirba, Yaadga, Bankui and Sourou; displacement strains health systems and water collection exposes women and girls to protection risks.

OCHA reports that the CERF drought framework covers Loroum, Oudalan, Séno and Yagha; its observational trigger was not activated in July–August, while national bulletins lacked province-level values and historical records needed for a formal alternate trigger.

OCHA's comparison reports late onset, rainfall 10–50% below normal, 7–10-day dry spells and low dam levels across the four framework provinces; at Dori in Séno, rainfall was 321 mm by 31 August versus a 414 mm 1991–2020 normal.

Oxfam and partners report four 2025–2027 drought anticipatory-action plans for Santéna (Boussouma), Damesma (Kaya), Somiaga (Ouahigouya) and Zougoungou (Gomponsom), developed with community vulnerability-and-capacity assessments and triggers using ANAM forecasts, PRESASS analysis and community early-warning observations.

The four plans envisage adapted agricultural inputs, food assistance, hygiene and dignity kits, heat-protection kits and income-generating support for vulnerable households; Oxfam says several thousand people are targeted.

known_gaps.text: Automated machine-screening is not independent source verification. Routine/default app-use approval does not certify claims or sources. 25 of 25 evidence records and 5 of 5 pathways lack claim-level verification in this remediation; review the linked records before relying on them.
The bank lacks a complete numeric climate baseline and scenario set for heat, drought, rainfall, and flood hazards at national and subnational scales.
Only the WFP portfolio provides independent response evaluation; unintended effects, distributional performance, and long-term adaptation or peace outcomes remain largely unevaluated.

The fcv-to-climate reverse pathway is supported mainly through access and service constraints; quantitative estimates of conflict's additional effect on climate losses and adaptation performance are absent.
OCHA reports that rainfall-station coverage is thinnest inside the Loroum–Oudalan–Séno–Yagha anticipatory-action area; Dori was the only listed station inside it.
The public Oxfam page summarizes four community plans, but the linked detailed plan PDFs could not be inspected, so local targeting, triggers and delivery performance remain unverified.
The accessed IMF climate-security statement is national-level; no new localized causal study linking specific rainfall or flood events to farmer-herder violence was accessed.
The searched sources document insecurity-related access and displacement, but do not quantify how insecurity changed climate adaptation delivery or climate-resilience outcomes in named places.
The national IMF climate-terrorism assertion was excluded: no new localized causal study was established.
September 2026 Karo Peli Phase 3! retains the assistance qualifier; early-2026 UNICEF need estimates are not treated as current October prevalence.
FEWS NET's named-region bird losses were not misattributed to rainfall; Dori station data were not extrapolated to other framework provinces.
Routine/default app-use approval granted by Lindsey Jones on 2026-10-27; independent source verification remains incomplete. Lending eligibility is not an FCV classification.
